sentences.text: Lonchidion minimorsus is a small hybodont shark species that lived during the Late Triassic period.
Its type locality is the Chinle Formation in Arizona, United States.
The low-crowned teeth are suited for crushing hard prey, indicating a durophagous diet.
Lonchidion is thought to have been euryhaline, able to inhabit both freshwater and brackish environments.
The species belongs to the family Lonchidiidae, an extinct group of hybodont sharks, and is placed in the class Chondrichthyes.
The genus Lonchidion has a fossil record from the Carnian to the Maastrichtian, spanning 237 to 66 million years ago, and persisted until the very end of the Cretaceous.
Some researchers argue that Lonchidion may not be a valid genus, suggesting its teeth could represent juvenile hybodont morphology.
